prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1270; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was operating a sedan northbound on a residential roadway in Katy, Texas, when the vehicle collided head-on with a sedan traveling southbound driven by Driver 2. Officers arrived to find both vehicles stopped in the travel lanes with front-end damage consistent with a low-speed frontal impact. Driver 1 was at the scene and reported neck pain consistent with whiplash, and the reported symptoms appear fitting for the type and force of this collision. Driver 1's presence in the vehicle at the time of the crash was confirmed by officers and by statements from others at the scene. A Passenger was not present. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several details of the collision, including the positions of the vehicles and the damage to their front bumpers, hoods and grilles. No independent witnesses were located who saw the moment of impact. The damage observed on both vehicles matches the account given by the drivers. Nothing in the vehicle's condition or in the available records suggests prior damage to the vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle involved.
